summary: Frontier video generation models work in a VAE latent space that compresses video in both space and time. This compression made training tractable, but now limits high-resolution, controllable, and interactive generation -- doubling resolution quadruples token count, conditions apply to groups of frames rather than individual ones, and each response must wait for the rest of its multi-frame block.
takeaways: PixVid keeps the diffusion transformer and replaces the VAE decoder with a convolutional head that renders its outputs into pixels.
We present PixVid, a simple yet effective method that lifts a pretrained latent video model to directly generate every frame in pixel space.

This compression made training tractable, but now limits high-resolution, controllable, and interactive generation -- doubling resolution quadruples token count, conditions apply to groups of frames rather than individual ones, and each response must wait for the rest of its multi-frame block.
